questions.q: When HR reports the New Hire Onboarding flow is "stuck," what's the right first move?
options: Open the execution log and find the specific run for the affected new hire record
Immediately delete and rebuild the flow from scratch
Assume the flow logic is broken and start rewriting its actions
Ask HR to manually complete every onboarding task instead
questions.explain: Since the flow has worked for other new hires, the log for this specific run is the fastest way to find the real cause.

questions.q: What did the execution log actually show for Maria Chen's run?
options: The flow crashed with a script error on its first action
The run was marked waiting, paused at a Manager Approval action
The run never started at all
The run completed successfully with no issues
questions.explain: The run was paused, not failed — it was legitimately waiting on an approval response that would never arrive.

questions.q: What did inspecting the approver data pill reveal?
options: It resolved to an administrator account instead of a manager
It resolved correctly to Maria's actual manager
It pointed to a manager in a different department entirely
It resolved to empty, because Maria's manager field was blank on her User record
questions.explain: The flow tried to route to her manager as designed, but that field had no value for this record.

questions.q: What was the real root cause of the stuck onboarding flow?
options: A bug in the flow's Approval action logic
A data quality issue upstream — Maria's manager field was never populated
An expired IntegrationHub credential alias
A data type mismatch in an If/Else condition
questions.explain: The flow performed exactly as designed; the defect was in the data it was given, not its logic.

questions.q: What did the durable part of the fix add to the flow?
options: A longer timeout before the approval is considered stalled
A notification to HR every time any flow pauses
A removal of the Approval action entirely
A check for a blank manager field before the Approval action, routing to a default fallback approver when it's empty
questions.explain: This protects future new hires with the same data gap from silently stalling with nobody notified.
